public_rationale: Alphabet's filing for the period ended June 30, 2026, available July 23, says depreciation starts when assets are ready for their intended use [e1]. It describes broad infrastructure assets awaiting service but does not identify tens of billions of dollars in uninstalled GPUs or measure their installation rate [e1]. Its depreciation figures do not establish an increase caused by deploying that GPU inventory [e1]. This evidence therefore leaves both conditions unverified and cannot settle the forecast for Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Meta [e1].
limitations: The evidence covers Alphabet only and does not establish either condition for the four named companies.
Assets awaiting service include buildings and other infrastructure, not just GPUs.
Alphabet's six-month depreciation totals do not supply the required company-specific quarterly comparisons.
The forecast supplies no deadline or numerical definitions of slow installation and dramatic growth.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If hyperscalers hold tens of billions of dollars in uninstalled GPUs that are being installed slowly, their depreciation expenses will grow dramatically.
conditions: if hyperscalers hold tens of billions of uninstalled GPUs

statement.excerpt: If Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Meta are sitting on tens of billions of yet-to-be-installed GPUs, and said GPUs are only being installed at a snail’s pace every quarter, that means that these depreciation figures are set to grow dramatically.
statement.document_title: Where Are All The Data Centers?

from_speaker: If Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Meta
tens of billions of yet-to-be-installed GPUs
only being installed at a snail’s pace every quarter
these depreciation figures are set to grow dramatically
our_interpretation: Both the uninstalled GPU inventory and slow installation conditions must be established before scoring the forecast.
The ordinary reading is a substantial subsequent increase in the named companies' quarterly depreciation charges as the inventory enters service.
The comparison baseline is each company's latest reported quarter before May 12, 2026.
Each company's quoted depreciation series must be followed separately. Depreciation alone and depreciation plus amortization cannot be substituted for one another.
No numerical growth threshold or deadline is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: After both antecedents are verified, comparable company disclosures show a substantial increase in the relevant quarterly depreciation charges associated with placing the identified GPU inventory into service.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After both antecedents are verified and the identified inventory has entered service, comparable disclosures show that the predicted substantial increase did not occur. A short interval without growth is insufficient for this undated forecast.

evidence.locator: Form 10-Q, page 52, Capital Expenditures and Leases
evidence.explanation: The filing establishes the recognition mechanism behind the forecast. It does not establish tens of billions of uninstalled GPUs, their installation rate, or the predicted outcome across the four companies.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Records establishing the ownership, cost and quarterly installation rate of the specified GPU inventory for the named companies. Once both conditions are verified, comparable quarterly disclosures must show whether deployment causes a substantial depreciation increase against each company's latest reported quarter before May 12, 2026. Each comparison must retain the quoted expense series and account for retirements, useful-life changes and other assets. A clearly substantial increase attributable to deployment would support the forecast; completed deployment conclusively without that increase
